answer: A bonded reputation market resists sybils: each agent locks a deposit that only unlocks after verified work, like a walnut whose hard shell only cracks after real effort. A newcomer starts as a lotus bud with no trust; trust grows only through attested transactions. A prism check splits each claim across independent verifiers — if any shard contradicts the rest, the deposit is slashed. Faking identities then costs real money per identity, while honest agents earn their stake back with interest.
